can recognize them as miraculous who experiences their
impact upon himself. They do not furnish proofs, for anyone
is free to elude their efficacy, may indeed become scandalized
by them; for it is often the case that they do not fit into the
plan of the world's life, into its pedagogic or sociological and
political schemes, into the efficient organization of things.
They have no other ground than the fact that they have been
inspired by the preaching of the Gospel.
For the real miracle is just this—that the good news of
Christ is preached to the poor. The poor; that is to say, those
who suffer in this visible world and who wait for the world
to come. And what is the message preached to them? It may
be summed up in one word: freedom from the present world.
The Gospel has the power to free us from the oppression of
the world, because it is the message of God's grace and the
forgiveness of sins. It tells us that we become free from the
world and from ourselves, when we honestly and un-
reservedly commit ourselves to God who assures us of His
grace, in the word and the person of Jesus Christ.
The Word of God's grace makes all things new for the
believer. He who is to come has in truth come and has
renewed the world, for those who allow their being to be
renewed and transformed by Him. "Therefore if any one is
in Christ, he is a new creation" (2 Cor. 5: 17). Now there
exists the possibility of the total renewal of humanity, and
to one whose being is thus renewed, the world too is
renewed. "The light of eternal life shines here and gives the
world a new appearance." In what way has the world
become new? Paul describes this transformation of the
world when he paints the picture of the true servants of God:
they live their life and fulfil their ministry "through great
endurance, in afflictions, hardships, calamities, beatings,
imprisonments, tumults...; by purity, knowledge, for-
bearance, kindness, the Holy Spirit, genuine love, truthful
speech and the power of God; with the weapons of righteous-
ness for the right hand and for the left; in honour and dis-
